route_definitions.computer_use: Operate a live desktop, browser, or application GUI via screenshots, mouse clicks, keyboard input, or window automation.
route_definitions.visual_analysis: Read-only inspection or comparison of images, screenshots, UI mockups, or design frames without writing UI code or clicking a live GUI.
route_definitions.frontend_implementation: Implement or style UI components, layouts, CSS, React/Vue/Tkinter views, or visual interactions in code.
route_definitions.general_implementation: Implement, modify, or refactor backend, CLI, service, or library code in a repository.
route_definitions.debug_review: Diagnose a bug, race condition, crash, or regression; fix an isolated defect; OR perform a read-only code/diff/release/security review or independent audit.
route_definitions.exploration_analysis: Read-only codebase exploration, dependency mapping, log/telemetry forensics, or architectural tracing.
route_definitions.research_packet: Execute a quantitative experiment, backtest, statistical evaluation, or benchmark script and report metrics.
route_definitions.web_research: Survey public documentation, vendor specs, open-web articles, historical/cultural motifs, or academic literature and synthesize findings (even if the output is saved to a local Markdown path).
route_definitions.text_in_text_out: Draft, translate, polish, or restructure self-contained text, narrative dialogue, documentation, or copy when the needed source material is already in the brief.
route_definitions.self_contained_code: Write or verify a standalone algorithm, data structure, or script whose specification/inputs are self-contained in the brief without needing un-inlined local repository modules.
route_definitions.bounded_bulk_work: Apply a uniform, mechanical transformation or checklist across many files or items.
route_definitions.tool_execution: Run an explicit operational runbook, build/release pipeline, or CLI command sequence.
route_definitions.complex_build_plan: Author a multi-phase engineering specification, system migration plan, or architectural blueprint before implementation.
route_definitions.direction_reasoning: High-depth mathematical proof/derivation, formal critique, or first-principles strategic/architectural paradigm design.

dimension_rubric.anti_inflation_rule: Score ONLY the functional work the worker must perform, never the length or Markdown structure of the brief. Coordinator headers (`Parent session agent ID`, `工作目录: E:/...`), role docs, `AGENTS.md`/`SKILL.md` references, communication rules, and output/receipt file paths (`docs/.../report.md`, `output.json`) are dispatch boilerplate—ignore them when scoring `context_scale`, `reasoning_depth`, and `code_complexity`.
dimension_rubric.local_only_positive_vs_negative:
CRITICAL CONTRAST RULE for `local_only`:
- Set `local_only: true` when the task explicitly depends on existing files, directories, or repositories on THIS machine (reading, copying, searching, editing, building, or running tests against un-inlined local files/directories) or on local processes/daemons/GUI/environment.
- Set `local_only: false` whenever all required inputs are self-contained in the brief or fetched from the public internet: (a) `web_research` (public web/vendor/cultural/motif research, even if the brief specifies a local path like `docs/research/xxx.md` where the finished report will be saved); (b) `self_contained_code` (writing a standalone script/algorithm whose spec or input snippet is inlined in the brief, even if a target filename is named); (c) `text_in_text_out`, `direction_reasoning`, or `complex_build_plan` when all required background context is already included in the brief text.
dimension_rubric.read_only_review: Any read-only code review, PR/diff inspection, release-readiness audit, or diagnostic report that writes NO production code MUST have `code_complexity: 0` (even when reviewing complex systems code), `work_kind: "debug_review"` (or `exploration_analysis`), and `hallucination_risk: 3`.
dimension_rubric.context_scale:
Count coupled functional modules the worker must reason across, NOT the number of file paths mentioned in the prompt:
- `1` (Single unit): Modifying/reviewing ONE primary functional module/script (plus its paired unit test file and any role/brief/output paths), OR any self-contained research/text/algorithm task, OR running a uniform command/checklist.
- `2` (Multi-module): Modifying or tracing interactions across 2 to 5 distinct coupled functional modules or datasets.
- `3` (System-wide): Whole-repository architecture, cross-subsystem refactoring (>5 modules), or multi-stage orchestrator lifecycle.
dimension_rubric.divergence:
Measure how open-ended the solution space is:
- `1` (Convergent): Known target, concrete feature spec, deterministic runbook, factual diff review, or fixing an already-isolated bug.
- `2` (Multi-hypothesis): Diagnosing an unknown root cause with 2+ competing hypotheses (intermittent bug, race condition, memory/CPU anomaly) or comparing bounded technical alternatives.
- `3` (Divergent / Creative): Open-ended creative ideation, cultural/motif research with gameplay/narrative/product scheme proposals, inventing a new architecture or scoring paradigm from first principles, or open-ended brainstorming with no single predetermined answer.
dimension_rubric.reasoning_depth:
Rate the cognitive depth required by the core problem:
- `1` (Routine): Executing an explicit command/checklist/runbook, trivial constant/config tweak, mechanical bulk replacement, or simple smoke check (even inside a long Markdown brief).
- `2` (Standard/Hard): Standard single- or multi-module feature implementation, bug diagnosis & fix, read-only PR/module review, or structured research synthesis.
- `3` (Coupled/Deep): Cross-module refactoring of an existing system with strict invariants, deep concurrency/state root-cause forensics across subsystems, or a migration/implementation plan inside an architecture that already exists.
- `4` (Frontier): Open-ended design that decides a whole product or system and has no reference solution, which the user always gives to the newest top-tier model: a new game's overall technical architecture, detailed game-system design (progression, combat, economy rules and formulas), ultra-low-latency network/VPS architecture, a new system's first-principles architecture; also formal mathematical proof/derivation, algorithmic lower-bound analysis, or frontier theoretical critique.
dimension_rubric.multi_task_vs_single_task: Set `multi_task: true` ONLY when the brief bundles 2+ independent deliverables that could be assigned to separate workers in parallel (e.g., fixing a backend bug AND translating unrelated docs). A single deliverable with sequential steps (`diagnose -> fix -> test -> report`) or a single research report covering multiple sub-questions is ONE task (`multi_task: false, task_count: "1"`).
dimension_rubric.realtime_loop: Set `realtime_loop: true` ONLY when the worker agent itself must stay inside a running external system's continuous observe-act loop across turns where slow per-turn model latency directly degrades the live outcome (e.g., personally operating a live game / dailies / dungeons / AFK loop, sniping tickets / courses / appointments / flash sales live, watching a live order book or API stream and placing orders in real time, polling a live page / App / API to act immediately when a target state appears, interacting with live-stream chat). Set `needs_gui` independently based on whether the loop operates a graphical interface (`needs_gui: true, needs_visual: true, work_kind: "computer_use"` for GUI/browser/emulator/window loops; `needs_gui: false, needs_visual: false, work_kind: "tool_execution"` for pure CLI/REST/WebSocket API loops). Set `realtime_loop: false` for ALL software engineering, frontend/backend implementation, bug fixing, UI design, performance optimization, root-cause diagnosis, log analysis, or one-off GUI actions—even when the task mentions real-time, polling, games, order books, dashboards, or flash sales (e.g., writing/fixing a ticket/game/automation script, implementing real-time page refresh or message push, fixing page polling logic, designing a live trading dashboard frontend, diagnosing client loop waits or refresh latency, adding a countdown modal or live-stream chat component, fixing flash-sale page CSS, analyzing game/AFK logs, or a one-shot GUI click/setting toggle).
